title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: transverse vibration of an Euler–Bernoulli rod EF of length a, simply supported ('stylo fixa') at both ends and at the midpoint L. This is the case λ = 1/2 of Euler's general rod with one intermediate support. On the previous page the frequency equation factors into sin(ω/2)·[(1+e^ω)sin(ω/2) − (e^ω−1)cos(ω/2)] = 0. This page treats the first factor.

§49 (end): sin(ω/2) = 0 gives ω = 2iπ. This coincides with case IV (a pinned–pinned rod) once ω/2 replaces ω, because each half has length a/2. Each half vibrates as an independent pinned–pinned span. The 'simple sounds' are ω²c√(2gb)/(πa²) = 4π, 16π, 36π, 64π, … (times c√(2gb)/a²). Euler's frequency normalisation evidently divides by π, i.e. it counts per half-period. These are two octaves (factor 4) above case IV, since frequency scales as 1/L².

§50: Euler substitutes into his general expressions for the coefficients α, β, γ, δ of the left span and α′, β′, γ′, δ′ of the right span. These multiply e^{uω}, e^{−uω}, sin uω, cos uω. Several coefficients become 0/0 because their denominators contain sin(ω/2) − cos(ω/2)tan ω.
- He shows this denominator equals [sin(ω/2)cos ω − cos(ω/2)sin ω]/cos ω = −sin(ω/2)/cos ω.
- At ω = 2iπ we have cos ω = 1 and sin(ω/2) = 0, so he multiplies every coefficient by sin(ω/2), i.e. renormalises the eigenvector.
- This gives α = β = δ = 0 and γ = −(1−e^ω)(e^ω−1).
- Continuing onto the next page: α′ = β′ = δ′ = 0 and γ′ = (e^ω−1)(1−e^ω) = −γ.

The mode is therefore y = ±C sin(ζ + tω²c√(2gb)/a²)·sin(uω), with opposite signs on the two spans. This is the antisymmetric mode, with zero moment and nonzero slope at L.
errors: No substantive error. The removal of the 0/0 by multiplying through by sin(ω/2) is a heuristic normalisation rather than a limit argument, but it gives the correct eigenvector. The frequency list (4π, 16π, …) reflects Euler's convention of dividing ω² by π; it is not a missing square.

ideas.what: Factorisation of the frequency equation of a symmetric two-span beam into antisymmetric modes (each span pinned–pinned) and symmetric modes (each span pinned–clamped, tan x = tanh x)
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric/antisymmetric mode decomposition of a continuous beam on three supports
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E526) as an early treatment; standard in later structural dynamics (Rayleigh, Theory of Sound, etc.)
ideas.where_published: E526 itself (Acta Acad. Petrop. 1779/1782); discussed in Truesdell's 1960 survey of the history of elastic rods (Opera omnia II.11)

ideas.what: Scaling of flexural frequencies with 1/L², so that halving the length raises the pitch two octaves
Renormalising eigen-coefficients that become 0/0 at eigenvalues by multiplying through by the vanishing factor
ideas.modern_name: Eigenvector extraction from adjugate/cofactor expressions at a root

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine worked case of a known paper. The antisymmetric two-span mode is correctly identified and the result is standard and credited.
transcription_corrections: In the identity line the transcription has 'cos.½ tang.ω'. The printed text also omits ω there; the intended expression is cos ½ω · tang ω.
The sound numbers 4π, 16π, 36π, 64π are as printed; they are not a misreading of π².
